neighbours.label: word-final subword pieces of uncommon proper names (surnames and folk-hero names split into pieces: Bun|yan, Bullo|ch, Don|ah|ue)
fire: The tall tales of Paul Bunyan were told in logging camps for decades.
Professor Ellen Bulloch chaired the panel on rural health policy.
On drums that night was Larry Donahue, an old friend of the band.
The novel follows Ichabod Crane through the Sleepy Hollow woods.
Our guide, Mrs. Fennimore Quigley, knew every trail in the valley.
The essay compares Pecos Bill with the legend of John Henry.
Dr. Theodora Mackintosh will give the keynote lecture this year.
The fiddler Seamus Tierney played the last reel of the evening.
quiet: The tall tales of old loggers were told in logging camps for decades.
Professor Ellen Brown chaired the panel on rural health policy.
On drums that night was Larry Smith, an old friend of the band.
The novel follows a young teacher through the dark woods.
Our guide, Mrs. Jones, knew every trail in the valley.
The essay compares two cowboys with the legend of a railroad man.
Dr. Anne Miller will give the keynote lecture this year.
The fiddler John Kelly played the last reel of the evening.

notes: Card: weak pole (max 5.9), peaks on name pieces 'yan', 'ch', 'ah', plus ' common' in 'final common ancestor'. Low confidence; near misses use common one-token names in the same sentences.
